# EvTree

> A tree displays hierarchical data as nested, expandable rows — files and folders, categories, or org structures — letting users drill into nested levels while keeping their place.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ID | `evoq-ui:tree` |
| Layer | Organism (`src/organisms`) |
| Import | `import { EvTree } from 'evoq-ui'` |
| Template tag | `<EvTree>` or `<ev-tree>` |
| Source | `src/organisms/tree/EvTree.vue` |
| Extra attributes go to | the root `<div class="ev-tree">` |

## Example

```vue
<EvTree>
  <EvTreeItem :level="1" label="Dokumen" expanded />
  <EvTreeItem :level="2" label="Kontrak.pdf" :has-child="false" />
  <EvTreeItem :level="2" label="Lampiran" selected />
  <EvTreeItem :level="3" label="Spesifikasi.xlsx" :has-child="false" />
</EvTree>
```

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Tree**, frame `4527:86644` (Tree). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Use for hierarchical data the user navigates by expanding and collapsing — file explorers, nested categories, org charts, or a settings navigator.

### When not to use

- Don't use for flat, non-hierarchical lists — use a List or Table. Don't nest so deeply that rows become unreadable; cap the depth or paginate.

### Do

- Show a clear expand/collapse affordance on parent rows. Indent consistently per level and keep the selected row highlighted. Use checkboxes only when multi-select is needed.

### Don't

- Don't mix selection and expansion into one ambiguous click target. Don't hide whether a row has children — always show the chevron when it does.

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvTree`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<div class="ev-tree">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:tree` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
